paper_title: Cool-3D: An End-to-End Thermal-Aware Framework for Early-Phase Design Space Exploration of Microfluidic-Cooled 3DICs

extraction.paper_title: Cool-3D: An End-to-End Thermal-Aware Framework for Early-Phase Design Space Exploration of Microfluidic-Cooled 3DICs

scenario.figure_or_table: Table VI and Fig. 9 (baseline chip, Splash2 fft, steady-state HotSpot 7.0 heat maps)
scenario.description: Baseline 3-layer 3DIC (bottom core layer with 4 cores and shared L2, two 4x4 memory-bank layers above) with a passive heat sink and no microfluidic cooling, evaluated with the gem5 + McPAT + CACTI-3DD + HotSpot 7.0 Cool-3D flow. Heat maps per layer are shown for the fft benchmark, with maximum temperatures of 395.52 K, 392.83 K and 390.57 K for the core, middle memory and top memory layers.
scenario.architecture: 4 out-of-order 8-issue cores at 2 GHz; L1 I/D caches 4KB/8KB 2-way; shared 2MB L2; 8GB memory with 32 banks (8 banks per rank); 3 layers: bottom cores 0-3 (2x2), middle memory banks 0-15 (4x4), top memory banks 16-31 (4x4)
scenario.workload: Splash2 fft benchmark (default problem size) from the Splash2 suite
scenario.operating_point: Passive heat sink, no microfluidic cooling; steady-state thermal simulation; 2 GHz core clock; per-block power values and floorplan dimensions are not given numerically in the paper

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 7.0 steady-state thermal simulation (pdf p.9-10), fed by gem5 performance, McPAT core/cache power and CACTI-3DD memory power
original_setup.optimizer: None; no automatic optimizer. Design changes are made manually in case studies (stacking order, microfluidic cooling pattern, L2 size). RL-based optimization is listed as future work (pdf p.13)
original_setup.controller: None; no dynamic thermal management or runtime controller is described. Steady-state analysis only
original_setup.benchmark: Baseline 3-layer 3DIC (bottom: 4 cores + shared L2; middle and top: 4x4 memory-bank layers), 4 O3 8-issue cores at 2 GHz, passive heat sink, no microfluidic cooling, running Splash2 fft at default problem size (Table VI pdf p.9; Fig. 9 pdf p.10)

thermal_observable.location: Bottom core layer (cores 0-3) of the baseline stack, Splash2 fft, from the Fig. 9 heat map (pdf p.10); the middle memory layer maximum is 392.83 K and the top memory layer maximum is 390.57 K
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum temperature over the layer's heat map in the steady-state HotSpot 7.0 simulation, as labelled in the figure. The paper uses the maximum over the whole 3D stack as its comparison metric in Case Study I (pdf p.10)

physical_mismatches.reason: Paper provides no numeric floorplan geometry (x, y, width, height) for any block; Fig. 9 shows only a labelled heat-map layout with no dimensions, and die area is not stated. A Studio floorplan cannot be built without inventing coordinates.
Paper provides no per-block power values for the fft baseline; McPAT and CACTI-3DD outputs are not tabulated, and total chip power is not given. Splitting power would require an unpublished rule.

The scenario is a 3-layer 3D stack with a core layer under two memory layers. A 2D or single-die Studio model cannot represent the vertical stacking, layer-to-layer coupling, or the 3D layer-ordering effects the paper studies.

Cooling in the baseline is a passive heat sink whose HotSpot 7.0 package parameters are not published. Case studies II-III add microfluidic cooling layers (vertical and 90-degree bent channels), which a Studio model may not support.

The original flow chains gem5, McPAT, CACTI-3DD, and HotSpot 7.0, with per-block power derived from workload simulation. Studio cannot reproduce that upstream power generation, so the thermal solve is only an approximation of the HotSpot 7.0 step.
The paper has no transient, controller, optimizer, or reliability component in the selected baseline scenario, so there is no mismatch from those; only a steady-state solve is relevant.

methods.note: Text on pp.3, 5, 6 and 9-10 supports the described flow: gem5, McPAT, CACTI-3DD memory power and HotSpot 7.0. It also supports the steady-state heat maps for the baseline chip and the three-layer stack with a passive heat sink. This covers the method description only. It does not establish that the paper's results can be reproduced.

code.note: The only code links are the Cool-3D GitHub repo (pp.1, 13) and the Splash2 repo (p.14). The paper says the Cool-3D release is 'in the process of being released'. The packet bundles no assets (assets=[]), so no repo content, config, parser or script was inspected. A bare URL is not evidence. The Splash2 repo holds benchmark source, not thermal inputs.

parameters.note: Table VI values (4 cores, 2 GHz, 8-issue OoO, L1 4KB/8KB 2-way, L2 2MB, 8GB, 32 banks, 8 banks/rank, 3 layers) are verified in the text. The unit conversions are arithmetically correct. The L1 I-cache=4KB and D-cache=8KB assignment is inferred from the 'I/D' label and is not confirmed. The decisive thermal parameters are absent: die area, layer thicknesses, heat-sink, spreader and TIM properties, ambient temperature, grid resolution, and per-block power.

config.note: No HotSpot 7.0 config, floorplan files, gem5 or McPAT or CACTI-3DD configs, or front-end input for the baseline are provided in the paper or the packet. Table VI only names a 'passive heat sink'. The heat-sink side and package are not published. The experiment is typed custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan, which does not match the 3D stacked scenario.

data.note: The printed Fig. 9 maxima (395.52, 392.83, 390.57 K) and the 5.87x core0 ratio are present in the pdftotext output. The paper gives no numeric floorplan geometry for the core blocks, L2 or B_0-B_31, and no same-scenario power for any block in the fft baseline. The floorplan and power_w are empty, so the requirement that every block has power is not met. The heat-map figures were seen only as extracted text labels and were not rendered or visually verified.

findings.reason: The experiment is typed custom_2d_steady, but the scenario is a 3-layer 3D stack and the extraction itself says steady_2d_relevant=false. The 3D vertical coupling and layer ordering are decisive for the paper's observable, so any 2D framing would misrepresent it. With an empty floorplan, nothing is actually reproduced.

findings.reason: None of the three links was supplied as a pinned asset or inspected. The paper says the release is in process. The Splash2 URL is broken across a line in the PDF text, and the cleaned form 'splash2benchmark' is a reconstruction. These links are not evidence of configs, floorplan or power data.

Statements that a Studio model 'may not support' microfluidic layers or cannot represent 3D stacking are about a tool outside the packet. They are unsupported by the paper and unverified. The paper-grounded mismatch is the missing inputs.

The baseline text says the core layer is at the bottom and that heat is hard to release from the backside. It never states which side the heat sink is on. The extraction acknowledges this, so the boundary condition is unresolved for any reproduction.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate blocked the run for three reasons. The custom 2D steady experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w, so it fails the 1-128 block requirement. The paper supplies no numeric block geometry, per-block power, die area, or HotSpot 7.0 package parameters. The extracted evidence also lacks valid page or pinned-asset locators. The scenario is the Cool-3D baseline: a 3-layer 3DIC (cores under two memory layers) with a passive heat sink, running Splash2 fft in a steady-state HotSpot 7.0 solve. The paper's printed layer maxima are 395.52 K (core), 392.83 K (middle memory) and 390.57 K (top memory). Because Studio produced no result, there is no Studio temperature to compare, so comparison_valid is false. No numerical comparison or replication claim is made. Qualitatively, the paper shows the core layer hottest, and the core0 instruction ratio of 5.87x suggests a concentrated hotspot. This is only a reported observation from the paper, not something verified here. This is a custom steady run, so there is no transient trace, and the paper's baseline has no transient, controller, or optimizer component. The final verdict is no simulation and no valid comparison.
limitations: Studio was not run because the gate requires 1-128 blocks and a power_w object; the extracted floorplan and power are empty.
